title: Smart Queue & Feedback Management System MVP

requirements.text: Implement backend data models and APIs for a digital queue: create/list services, join a service queue, leave a queue, fetch a user’s current queue status (position + state), and fetch the current queue snapshot for a service.
acceptanceCriteria: A service can be created and is returned by a list-services API.
A user can join a service queue and receives a queue entry identifier (or equivalent).
A user can request their status and receive at minimum: serviceId, current position (1-based), and a status state (e.g., waiting/served/cancelled).
A user can leave/cancel their queue entry and subsequent status calls reflect cancellation.
Queue order is deterministic (FIFO) and stable across canister upgrades/restarts using stable storage.

requirements.text: Implement backend staff/admin queue controls for a service: advance to next customer (serve current), mark an entry as no-show/cancelled, and reset/clear a service queue.
acceptanceCriteria: Advancing the queue updates the head entry to a terminal state (served) and the next waiting entry becomes position 1.
No-show/cancel operations remove the entry from the waiting order and positions update accordingly.
Reset/clear removes all active entries for a given service.
Admin-only operations are authorization-protected (e.g., allowlist of admin principals stored in backend state/config).

requirements.text: Implement backend feedback collection APIs: submit feedback for a service (rating + free-text comment), and list feedback entries per service (admin/staff view).
acceptanceCriteria: Users can submit feedback containing at minimum: serviceId, rating (bounded numeric), optional comment text, and timestamp.
Feedback is persisted in stable storage and remains after canister upgrades.
Admin/staff can list feedback for a given service ordered by newest first.

requirements.text: Build a user-facing frontend that lets users: (1) select a service, (2) join the queue, (3) view live-refreshed queue status (position + status), and (4) leave the queue.

quotes: users can join a digital queue, track their position

acceptanceCriteria: There is a clear flow to select a service and join its queue.
After joining, the UI displays the user’s current position and status state.
The UI provides a cancel/leave action and updates state after completion.
Queue status view refreshes via polling (React Query) at a reasonable interval (e.g., every 5–10 seconds) and supports manual refresh.

requirements.text: Build a user-facing feedback UI: users can select a service, submit a rating and optional comment, and see a confirmation/receipt state after successful submission.
acceptanceCriteria: Feedback form includes a rating control and a comment field (comment optional).
Submission errors are shown in English with actionable guidance.
On success, the form resets and shows a confirmation message in English.

requirements.text: Add an admin/staff frontend area to manage queues and review feedback: choose a service, view current queue entries, advance/serve next, mark no-show/cancel, clear queue, and view feedback list.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin view shows a service selector and a queue list (ordered) with each entry’s state.
Admin actions (advance, no-show/cancel, clear) trigger backend updates and the UI reflects changes.
Admin view includes a feedback list per service (rating, comment, timestamp).
If the user is not authorized as admin, admin actions are disabled or the admin view is hidden with a clear English message.

requirements.text: Apply a cohesive, creative visual theme across the frontend (colors, typography, spacing, and components) suitable for a “service queue” product, avoiding blue/purple as primary brand colors.
acceptanceCriteria: The app uses a consistent palette (primary/secondary/background/text) and typographic scale across pages.
Primary brand color is not blue or purple.
Layout is consistent (header/nav, content widths, card styles) across Queue, Feedback, and Admin areas.

requirements.text: Add required static generated images to the frontend and render them in the UI (store under frontend/public/assets/generated).
acceptanceCriteria: All required generated images exist under frontend/public/assets/generated with the specified filenames.
At least the logo is used in the app header and the hero illustration is used on the landing/home screen.
Images are loaded as static assets (no backend image serving).

constraints: Use English for all user-facing text.
Backend must remain a single Motoko actor (no additional backend services).
Do not edit files under frontend/src/components/ui or other immutable paths; compose UI components instead.
nonGoals: Payments, ticket scanning/QR codes, SMS/email notifications.
Third-party authentication providers other than Internet Identity.

required: Minimal modern logo mark featuring a queue/ticket motif (sqfm-logo.dim_256x256.png)
Wide hero illustration showing people in an organized line with abstract UI elements, warm neutral palette with teal/orange accents (sqfm-hero.dim_1200x600.png)
